title: Writing Good Prompts
about: Ask AI for what you want with a clear goal, context and format.

cards.prompt: What you type is a **prompt**. Is each one **vague**, or **clear** about what it wants and what shape?

items.label: Tell me all about rivers, please!

cards.hint: Does it say exactly what it wants, and how long or what shape?
cards.nudge: A long or polite prompt can still be vague. Which say exactly what, and what shape?
cards.explanation: The clear ones give a **goal** (explain, titles) and a **format** (3 sentences, 3 titles). "Tell me all about rivers, please!" is polite but vague: all of what, and how long?

cards.title: What a good prompt says
cards.body:
A chatbot writes likely words to follow **your** text, so the more you say, the better it aims. Say:

- **The goal:** what you want done.
- **The context:** who it's for, what you already have.
- **The format:** how long, what shape.

Ask "Tell me about dogs" when you wanted puppy tips? Enjoy 2,000 words on poodle history.

cards.prompt: Is each bit of a prompt the **goal**, the **context** or the **format**?
cards.hint: Goal: what to do. Context: who it's for, or what you have. Format: shape or length.
cards.nudge: Ask: is it a job to do, a fact about you or your situation, or the answer's shape?
cards.explanation: **Goals** say what to do (summarise, plan). **Context** says who it's for or what you know (your brother, chapter 1). **Format** is the shape (a rhyme, a table).

cards.prompt: **"Write a summary of the water cycle."** has a goal. What would improve it **most**?

options.text: Asking it to include lots of facts and examples
options.nudge: More facts makes it longer, not better aimed. Who's it for, and what shape?

options.text: Asking it to check its facts before it answers
options.nudge: Asking doesn't make it check, and it still doesn't say who it's for or how long.

options.text: Saying please, and that it's really important
options.nudge: Politeness and urgency don't say who it's for, or how long.

options.text: Saying who it's for and how long it should be

cards.hint: Check it against the three parts of a good prompt. Which are missing?
cards.explanation: It has a **goal**, but no **context** (who's it for?) and no **format** (one paragraph? five bullets?). The other options add neither.

cards.prompt: You're giving a 1-minute talk about octopuses at your nature club.

steps.text: You type "octopus facts" and get 20 long paragraphs. What do you change?

choices.text: Ask "octopus facts" again, and hope for better
choices.consequence: Another 20 paragraphs. Nothing you said changed, so nothing useful changed.

choices.text: "3 surprising octopus facts for a 1-minute talk"
choices.consequence: Much better: three short, surprising facts. One says an octopus has "nine brains".

choices.text: Turn the temperature up for more interesting facts
choices.consequence: Stranger facts, some nonsense. Temperature changes how it picks, not what it knows.

steps.text: "Nine brains" sounds amazing. What do you do before using it?

choices.text: Check it on a trusted science website
choices.consequence: Close: an octopus has one central brain plus a cluster of nerve cells in each of its 8 arms. You say that.

choices.text: Use it: a good prompt gives good facts
choices.consequence: A good prompt aims the answer; it doesn't check it. Surprising facts most need checking.

cards.hint: Which parts was "octopus facts" missing? Does a better prompt make facts true?
cards.explanation: Saying the **goal, context and format** turned 20 paragraphs into 3 useful facts. But surprising facts still need **checking** in a trusted source.

cards.prompt: Paste in your notes, but keep private details out: chats may be stored. Should each go **in** or be **left out**?
cards.hint: Does it help aim the answer, and is it safe and yours to share?
cards.nudge: Some come with a helpful-sounding reason. Is that worth sharing something private?
cards.explanation: Who it's for, the length and your notes help it aim. Your address and password stay private (name your suburb instead), and a friend's private message isn't yours to share.

cards.prompt: "Give me facts about sharks" got a long, boring list. Which **one** change helps **most**?

options.text: "Lots of detailed, interesting facts about every shark"
options.nudge: Longer and keener, but how many facts, what for, and how long each?

options.text: "3 surprising shark facts for a class talk, 1 line each"
"Shark facts. Be accurate and double-check, no mistakes"
options.nudge: Asking for accuracy doesn't make it accurate, and it still lacks how many or what for.

options.text: "You're a shark expert. Tell me your most amazing facts"
options.nudge: That sets a style, but how many facts, for what, and how long?

cards.hint: Which parts of a good prompt was the original missing? Which option adds them?
cards.explanation: Only the class-talk prompt says **how many**, **what kind**, **what for** and **what shape**. The others sound keen, careful or expert, but don't aim the answer.

cards.prompt: You want a chatbot to quiz you on your history notes.

steps.text: You type "Quiz me" and get 10 questions, answers right underneath. Most generous quizmaster ever. Best fix?

choices.text: Cover the answers with your hand as you go
choices.consequence: It's easy to peek, and you didn't fix the prompt.

choices.text: "One question at a time; hide answers till I reply"
choices.consequence: Now it asks, waits and tells you if you're right. You said exactly what you wanted.

choices.text: "Make the questions much harder this time"
choices.consequence: Harder questions, answers still underneath. The prompt didn't say what was wrong.

steps.text: Forty questions later, it shows answers again: in a very long chat, a chatbot can lose track of the start. What now?

choices.text: Repeat your instruction: one at a time, answers hidden
choices.consequence: It goes back to asking and waiting: repeating put the instruction back in front of it.

choices.text: "Make the questions easier from now on"
choices.consequence: Easier questions, still with answers. The problem was the lost instruction.

choices.text: Keep going: it will remember the rule again soon
choices.consequence: The longer the chat, the further back your instruction. It won't come back by itself.

cards.hint: What exactly went wrong each time? Say that in your next prompt.
cards.explanation: When an answer isn't right, **say what was wrong**: here, the format. In a very long chat it can lose the start, so **repeat your instructions**.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- A good **prompt** says the **goal**, the **context** and the **format**.
- Paste in your notes or drafts, never private details.
- Long chat? It can lose the start, so repeat your instructions.

Next: checking AI's work.
